sections.h2: Where does a Lenawee County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, liens, surveys and land corners for property in Lenawee County are recorded at the county Register of Deeds in Adrian, the county seat. The office checks each document against Michigan recording requirements, records it, stores it digitally and mails the original back to whoever presented it unless told otherwise.

The county itself covers about 750 square miles of land in southeast Michigan, was carved out of Monroe County in 1822 and was organized in 1826. Adrian College and Siena Heights University sit inside its borders. A seller with a house near Adrian, Tecumseh or out in a farm township ends up at the same recording counter, because Michigan assigns deed recording to the county and leaves assessing and building rules to each city and township.

The office does not supply deed forms and its staff may not help fill one out. Content and intent belong to whoever prepares the document, so a title company or attorney normally handles the paperwork when a house sells.

sections.h2: How much does the Lenawee County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording a document costs $30.00 no matter how many pages it runs, according to the county's published answers. Copies of recorded documents are $1.00 per page at the counter. The office takes check, cash and credit card, and a card payment carries an extra access fee.

The county warns owners about commercial mailers that offer certified deed copies for as much as $83.00 each. The same document is available directly from the office for as little as $2.00, so a letter that looks official is worth checking against the county's own page before paying.

sections.h2: What makes the recorder reject a deed in Lenawee County?
sections.html:
The county lists 17 statutory requirements and calls them a guideline, since many instruments carry extra rules. The ones that trip up home sales most often are these:

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed under them, and the names must match the notary acknowledgment (MCL 565.201).
  • The first page needs a margin of at least 2.5 inches at the top, and every other edge needs at least half an inch.
  • Type must be black, at least 10-point, on white paper of 20-pound weight or heavier, sized from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The first line of print must name the recordable event, and one instrument may evidence only one such event.
  • The grantee's street or post office address and the name and address of the person who drafted the document must appear on the page.
  • A deed signed in Michigan needs acknowledgment before a judge, a court clerk or a notary public.
  • No more than the last four digits of a Social Security number may appear.

When a deed says "survivor", a certified death certificate must already be recorded and referenced by liber and page, or be recorded with the deed. Court orders have to be certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.

sections.h2: Does Lenawee County charge transfer tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Yes, on most sales for money. Michigan's state real estate transfer tax applies to deeds given for consideration, and under MCL 207.523 the seller or grantor owes it and pays it to the county treasurer where the land sits. The county has its own transfer tax under Act 134 of 1966. Ask the Register of Deeds for the combined rate on your sale price before closing, since the title company will normally collect it from the seller's proceeds.

Both statutes list instruments that escape the tax. Among them:

  • Deeds where the consideration is under $100.
  • A conveyance from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild (state tax exemption, MCL 207.526).
  • Court judgments or orders that order a transfer without a stated price.
  • Quitclaim deeds that only correct a flaw in title.
  • Land contracts, until legal title passes.
  • Deeds given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a mortgage.

The exemption has to be claimed correctly on the document, so a seller using one should have the title company confirm the wording first.

sections.h2: How do I search land records in Lenawee County?
sections.html:
The county runs an online land records search with two entry points. One is a full text search that reads typed or legible text and works on a phone. The other suits experienced users and searches by name, recorded date and liber and page; it works best on a computer with Chrome or Edge and pop-ups allowed. Search results are information only, and images are available once purchased.

A seller can use the name search to confirm what is recorded against a property before listing: the vesting deed, open mortgages, a surviving-spouse affidavit, or an old lien that was paid but never discharged. A buyer's title company runs the same search, so surprises found early save time later.

Owners who want a warning if someone records a document in their name can sign up for the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or by calling 1-800-728-3858.

sections.h2: How does recording fit into selling a house in Lenawee County?
sections.html:
The deed is the last step. The title company collects the signed and notarized deed at closing, pays the recording fee and any transfer tax, and sends the package to the Register of Deeds. Until it is recorded, the sale is not on the public record.

Property tax comes up in the same week. A new owner's taxable value is uncapped the year after a transfer, and the buyer files the property transfer affidavit with the local assessor. Appeals of an assessment go first to the local Board of Review in March and then to the Michigan Tax Tribunal, according to the county equalization office. Lenawee County also offers a summer tax deferment application through its treasurer, who keeps office hours from 8:00 to noon and 1:00 to 4:30 on weekdays.

If the house needs repairs, has back taxes or sits in an estate, a cash buyer can close without the repair requests that come with a financed purchase. The recording steps stay the same.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Lenawee County?
faqs.a: The county lists a flat $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. Transfer tax is separate and depends on the sale price, so ask the office or your title company for the figure on your sale.

faqs.q: Can the Lenawee County Register of Deeds help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not supply forms and its employees cannot advise on or help complete a document. A title company or attorney should prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Lenawee County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor is liable under MCL 207.523, and the tax goes to the county treasurer where the property is located. At a closing it usually comes out of the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: How can I get a copy of my deed without overpaying?
faqs.a: Ask the Register of Deeds directly. Copies are $1.00 per page at the counter, and the county says a deed can cost as little as $2.00, compared with up to $83.00 charged by commercial mailers.

faqs.q: Why was my Lenawee County deed rejected?
faqs.a: Common causes are copied rather than original signatures, margins that are too narrow, a missing drafter address, a name that differs from the notary block, or small print. Check the county's 17-point list before resubmitting.
